To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an epithelioid angiogenic sarcoma involving the splenetic capsule developed in a patient with retained gauze sponges in the left upper abdominal cavity for 38 years.
an epithelioid angioma of the splenic surface developed because of a foreign body.
a gauze foreign body retained for more than 30 years led to a splenic angiosarcoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms by which foreign bodies induce neoplasms.
the development of a new approach to the study of the effect of the splenic on the splenic capsule.
the study of the role played by the environment in carcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epithelioid angio-sarcoma in this report is a foreign body tumor, which developed in a splenic capsule scar following a nephrectomy.
this angiosarcomas of the splenic capsular region is a rare tumor, and the gauze sponge was the inert foreign body that induced this tumor.
the epithelioid angio-sarcoma of the spleen was caused by an inert gauze sponge retained for 38 yrs following left-sided nephroureterectomy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gauze sponge was the cause of the splenic epithelioid angio sarcoma, which developed because of its presence in the left upper quadrant for 38 years.
the presence of a gauzetextile sponge in the left flank for 38 years was the cause of the development of an epithelioid sarcoma of the splenicleft flank.
the epithelioid angio-sarcoma of the spleen, which we report, is a case of inert foreign body-induced tumorigenesis, which is a rare but real occurrence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

epithelioid angiomatosis, epithelioid hemangioendothelioma, and epithelioid angioendotheliomatosis can be differentiated from each other and from epithelioid angiocarcinomas by the presence of intracytoplasmic lumina and by immunohistochemical stains for endothelial cell markers.
a gauze spongectomy should be done at the time of nephrectomy, and that any retained gauze should be removed surgically as soon as possible.
the concept of inert tumorigenesis should be considered in the differential diagnosis of any neoplasm in a patient with a history of retained foreign bodies.
